title: 12-Factor Agents: Patterns of reliable LLM applications — Dex Horthy, HumanLayer
talk_summary: Dex Horthy argues that reliable production agents are mostly ordinary software: LLMs are stateless token-in/token-out functions, and quality comes from owning prompts, context construction, control flow, and state rather than delegating them to frameworks. He recommends small focused agent loops (3-10 steps) embedded in mostly deterministic DAGs, with explicit human-contact points and pause/resume via serialized state.

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the overall pipeline deterministic and insert small agent loops of roughly 3-10 steps only where judgment is needed, instead of one long autonomous loop over the whole workflow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you still have a mostly deterministic DAG and you have these very small agent loops with like three to 10 steps

takeaways.technique: Own and prune the context window
takeaways.what_they_do: Build the context window explicitly rather than blindly appending tool errors and stack traces; clear or summarize pending errors once a valid call succeeds.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you have errors and then you get a valid tool call, clear all the air pending errors out. Summarize them.

takeaways.technique: Serialize state and pause/resume for long tools
takeaways.what_they_do: When an agent calls a long-running tool, interrupt the loop, serialize the context window to a database keyed by a state ID, and resume by reloading and appending the result.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can interrupt the workflow, serialize that context window straight into a database because we own the context window

takeaways.technique: Natural-language intent token before tool call
takeaways.what_they_do: Force the model to emit a natural-language intent (done / need clarification / need human) as the first token before choosing a tool, so intent is decided in natural language rather than buried in tool-call selection.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you push the intent on that first token generation and the sampling to something that is natural language that the model understands

takeaways.technique: Hand-own prompts past a quality bar
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat prompts as owned source code and hand-write tokens once generated prompts plateau, because output reliability is determined by input tokens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the only thing that determines the reliability of your agent is how good of tokens can you get out

takeaways.technique: Deterministic gates around small LLM judgment steps
takeaways.what_they_do: Use deterministic CI/CD for the bulk of the pipeline and call the model only at the specific decision point, then return to deterministic code.
